agentProviderSpec.description: A compact provider selector: provider[-model[-effort]]. A plain provider id (see agentProvider) inherits the CLI's own model and effort; an optional model rides after the provider (passed to the CLI verbatim, so multi-segment ids like gpt-5.6-sol work); a trailing effort token (lo/low, med/medium, hi/high, xhi/xhigh, max) sets the reasoning effort. Examples: claude, codex-gpt-5.6-sol, claude-fable-hi, codex-gpt-6-astra-lo, opencode-local/qwen3-coder:30b. OpenCode native provider/model ids may include slashes and model tags. A model is rejected for providers without a model flag, and effort is checked against the provider's published vocabulary when one exists.

model.description: Opaque native model ID. OpenCode uses backend/model; suffixes are literal.

effort.description: Exact native effort or variant; no compact aliases are expanded.

visibility.description: Whether this workflow is offered as a choice. "internal" keeps the name out of every listing (the repo manifest, the desktop's new-task picker, the tool catalog's advertised lineup) while it still resolves when named explicitly on task creation — visibility governs listing, not access. Defaults to "public" when absent.

routing.description: How a stage's result chooses where the task goes. Omitted means "legacy": success follows the stage's transition policy and a review names a target stage through kanna_request_revision under the task-wide revision_limit. "exits" opts into named exits (spec §5): every stage has an implicit `advance` exit to the next stage, a stage may declare loop exits mapped to earlier stages, a session names one of its stage's exits in its result (never a stage), and each loop spends the destination stage's own budget. A workflow that uses exits, budget or loop_transition must declare "exits"; one that declares "exits" may not use revision_limit, revision_transition or plan_context.

budget.description: Routing "exits" only: the default budget of every stage that declares none -- how many agent-chosen loop exits may move the task back into that stage before a further one records its result and parks the task instead. Defaults to 5. 0 means agent loops into the stage always park. A person or manager sending the task back to a stage resets that stage's count.

plan_context.description: Planning context Kanna stamps onto a task's pinned workflow when a plan stage publishes the remaining stages through kanna_complete_stage. It is written by the server, never authored by hand: an edit that changes it is refused, and an edit that omits it carries the stamped value forward. Its `result` is bound to the reserved $PLAN_RESULT prompt variable for every stage and post of the extended workflow, so the approved plan stays reachable after later stages, revisions, resume, and recovery.

source_run_id.description: Stage run whose successful completion published this plan.

stage.description: Name of the stage that published the plan.

result.description: The full recorded stage result of that run, in the same shape $PREV_MAIN_RESULT carries.

request_digest.description: Fingerprint of the exact combined completion that published these stages: the recorded result together with the expected and requested definitions. A retry that matches it is the same operation replayed; one that differs is a different publication and is refused rather than silently ignored or applied over the stored one.

revision_limit.description: Legacy routing: agent-requested revision rounds a task may spend before Kanna stops forking revisions and parks the task for its human. Defaults to 5 when omitted; 0 disables the cap. A human-requested revision is never refused and resets the count. Routing "exits" budgets each destination stage instead (budget).

exits.description: Routing "exits" only: loop exits this stage's session may name in its result, each mapped to this stage or an earlier one, e.g. {"revise": "in progress", "replan": "plan"}. `advance` is implicit (the next stage) and cannot be declared. A loop exit taken with status success moves the task back to its destination, carries the result message there, and spends one unit of the destination's budget; any other status parks the task whatever exit is named.

budget.description: Routing "exits" only: agent-chosen loops back into this stage the task may take before a further one parks it. Overrides the workflow's budget (default 5); 0 means every agent loop into this stage parks. A person or manager sending the task back here resets the count.

revision_transition.description: Legacy routing: completion policy for main runs entered through a revision request. Defaults to transition when omitted. Routing "exits" uses loop_transition instead.

loop_transition.description: Routing "exits" only: how the task leaves this stage through its advance exit when the stage was re-entered by a loop. Defaults to transition. Independent of the stage's budget and of its first-entry transition.

post.description: Tail work injected into the stage's running agent session when the stage transitions forward. `agent` is the fallback spawned when the session is dead.
